newsitem.title: USA: Calif. misses $1 bln payments due to budget delay.
newsitem.headline: Calif. misses $1 bln payments due to budget delay.

text.p: The state of California has withheld more than $1 billion in payments from counties and businesses as a result of the legislature's budget standoff, the state's controller said Tuesday.

Controller Kathleen Connell said several major payments totaling over $1 billion, including payments to California's cash-strapped counties, already have been missed. More than $200 million is owed to counties from California's motor vehicle license fee, she said.
"It's very simple: No budget, no checks," Connell said in a statement.

An estimated 2,000 state legislative staffers will not receive their paychecks on Tuesday because of the budget impasse. Connell said she was also forced to withhold checks to vendors that work for the state.
"The political gaming going on in the Capitol is jeopardizing the fiscal livelihood of many innocent, hard-working individuals," she said.
California Governor Pete Wilson and leaders of the state Senate and Assembly do not plan to hold budget talks Tuesday, but could meet Wednesday to try to resolve the impasse, the officials said.
"They're moving very slowly," one legislative staffer said.
Welfare reform legislation has been the major stumbling block for lawmakers negotiating the state's spending plan for the 1997-1998 fiscal year, which began July 1.
The state's Constitutional budget deadline was June 15.
The state Assembly's budget committee on Monday rejected a bill that would have docked the pay of lawmakers whenever they are late enacting the state budget.
